!35 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// What to look for: DXC accepts a read of an uninitialised value and emits `undef` for it,\0A// with no error, when the read goes through a loop-carried phi node. The identical read\0A// written straight-line (the commented-out line) IS rejected by DXIL validation.\0A//\0A// In each DXC pane, find the loop body and read the accumulator's phi node: its incoming\0A// value from the loop preheader is the token `undef`, and the next line adds it into the\0A// running total with a floating-point add. Then look at what the compiler said: there is no\0A// error and DXIL validation passed. Trunk additionally warns\0A// (`parameter 'result' is uninitialized when used here [-Wparameter-usage]`), which\0A// dxc 1.6.2112 does not; the emitted DXIL is the same in both.\0A//\0A// To see the contrast the issue is actually about, uncomment the straight-line accumulation\0A// and delete the loop. DXC then reports \22Instructions should not read uninitialized value\22\0A// and refuses to produce a module. Same uninitialised read; diagnosed one way, silent\0A// the other.\0A//\0A// This is a compute restating of the vs_6_0 shader in the issue, so that Clang -- whose DXIL\0A// backend cannot lower vertex signature I/O -- can answer the same question on the same\0A// source. The stage-accurate original was measured locally and behaves identically.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// Issue 3811 -- compute restatement of repro.hlsl, for a Compiler Explorer session that all\0A// three compilers (dxc, dxc trunk, clang) can answer on the SAME source. Clang's DXIL backend\0A// cannot lower vertex signature I/O, so the vs_6_0 original would fill a Clang pane with noise\0A// about the stage rather than about this issue.\0A// The local, stage-accurate evidence is repro.hlsl at vs_6_0, exactly as filed.\0AStructuredBuffer<float> values : register(t0, space0);\0ARWStructuredBuffer<float> result_out : register(u0);\0A\0Avoid Accumulate(int count, out float result)\0A{\0A\09// result += values[0];  // <-- straight-line spelling: rejected by DXIL validation\0A\09for (int i = 0; i < count; i++)\0A\09\09result += values[i];  // <-- loop spelling: accepted\0A}\0A\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid main(uint3 tid : SV_DispatchThreadID)\0A{\0A\09float result = 0.0;\0A\09Accumulate((int)tid.x, result);\0A\09result_out[0] = result;\0A}\0A"}

!98 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// What to look for: DXC accepts a read of an uninitialised value and emits `undef` for it,\0A// with no error, when the read goes through a loop-carried phi node. The identical read\0A// written straight-line (the commented-out line) IS rejected by DXIL validation.\0A//\0A// In each DXC pane, find the loop body and read the accumulator's phi node: its incoming\0A// value from the loop preheader is the token `undef`, and the next line adds it into the\0A// running total with a floating-point add. Then look at what the compiler said: there is no\0A// error and DXIL validation passed. Trunk additionally warns\0A// (`parameter 'result' is uninitialized when used here [-Wparameter-usage]`), which\0A// dxc 1.6.2112 does not; the emitted DXIL is the same in both.\0A//\0A// To see the contrast the issue is actually about, uncomment the straight-line accumulation\0A// and delete the loop. DXC then reports \22Instructions should not read uninitialized value\22\0A// and refuses to produce a module. Same uninitialised read; diagnosed one way, silent\0A// the other.\0A//\0A// This is a compute restating of the vs_6_0 shader in the issue, so that Clang -- whose DXIL\0A// backend cannot lower vertex signature I/O -- can answer the same question on the same\0A// source. The stage-accurate original was measured locally and behaves identically.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// Issue 3811 -- compute restatement of repro.hlsl, for a Compiler Explorer session that all\0A// three compilers (dxc, dxc trunk, clang) can answer on the SAME source. Clang's DXIL backend\0A// cannot lower vertex signature I/O, so the vs_6_0 original would fill a Clang pane with noise\0A// about the stage rather than about this issue.\0A// The local, stage-accurate evidence is repro.hlsl at vs_6_0, exactly as filed.\0AStructuredBuffer<float> values : register(t0, space0);\0ARWStructuredBuffer<float> result_out : register(u0);\0A\0Avoid Accumulate(int count, out float result)\0A{\0A\09// result += values[0];  // <-- straight-line spelling: rejected by DXIL validation\0A\09for (int i = 0; i < count; i++)\0A\09\09result += values[i];  // <-- loop spelling: accepted\0A}\0A\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid main(uint3 tid : SV_DispatchThreadID)\0A{\0A\09float result = 0.0;\0A\09Accumulate((int)tid.x, result);\0A\09result_out[0] = result;\0A}\0A"}
